sections.title: Biology & biomedicine — 22 November 2026 announcement: 8 notable recent papers
sections.text: Eight notable recent papers in a batch dominated by computational biomolecular structure and dynamics, with spatial gene-expression reconstruction and biomedical measurement methods. Agenda: compare protein-modeling approaches, then review genomics, imaging, and translational assays. No official arXiv trending chart exists; the ranking is inferred from incomplete coverage and no independent attention signal was detected.

sections.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
sections.abstract: BioEmu2 is a generative model for atom-resolved biomolecular structures that aims to unify structure prediction, equilibrium sampling, and time propagation across protein, nucleic-acid, ligand, and ion-containing systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report competitive structure-prediction benchmarks, equilibrium samples with 0.7–1.2 kcal/mol free-energy errors against MD references, and time-propagation tests across 78 systems; some trajectories relax too quickly.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational comparisons to structures and molecular-dynamics references are not experimental validation. The authors state that slow binding, dissociation, folding, and unfolding kinetics are not established as quantitatively accurate in this release.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.25, entirely one cross-list (q-bio.BM); no HF or HN attention signal. Candidate-level Semantic Scholar values: 0 citations and 0 influential citations. Selected for direct biomolecular relevance, not popularity.

sections.title: Structural Agreement Indicates Prediction Accuracy For Protein-Ligand Co-Folding
sections.abstract: Across seven protein–ligand co-folding models, the authors evaluate ensemble structural agreement as a signal for whether predicted ligand poses are correct, and propose the CORE Score.
sections.claimed_contribution: In the Runs N’ Poses benchmark of 2,600 protein–ligand systems, the authors report mean ROC AUCs of 0.866 for top-1 success and 0.838 for oracle success, compared with 0.757 and 0.759 for ipTM.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective structural benchmark results are not prospective validation. The study evaluates pose correctness, not whether a compound binds or has an effect.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.25 from one q-bio.BM cross-list; no HF/HN attention or candidate-level Semantic Scholar citation record. Ranked for protein–ligand relevance.

sections.title: Hierarchical Hybrid-Coordinate Flow Matching for Accurate and Physically Plausible Apo-to-Holo Protein Generation
sections.abstract: CrypticFlow combines Cartesian anchor generation with recursive internal-coordinate decoding to predict holo-like conformations from apo protein structures while controlling local geometry.
sections.claimed_contribution: On a fixed 150-pair D3PM split and five training runs, the authors report improved local geometry (99.58% adjacent-distance fidelity) and mean direct RMSD of 2.766 Å; external CryptoBench results report modest improvement over the unchanged apo input.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the accuracy lead does not hold against all capacity-matched baselines. The predictor is effectively deterministic, ligand-free, and does not represent alternative holo states.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.25 from one q-bio.BM cross-list; no HF/HN attention signal. Selected for its structural-biology method and quantitative held-out evaluation.

sections.title: GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction
sections.abstract: GaLF-ST jointly learns Gaussian spatial fields, latent vectors, and a decoder to reconstruct multigene expression from sparse spatial-transcriptomics observations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors compare against four methods on seven dataset groups and three held-out fractions, reporting leading overall reconstruction performance and reduced runtime and GPU memory use.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is benchmark-based reconstruction; the abstract does not establish transfer to prospective tissues or experimental confirmation of inferred expression. Code and appendix are planned for a later version.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.25 from one q-bio.GN cross-list; no HF/HN attention signal. Ranked for direct genomics relevance.

sections.title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
sections.abstract: A stochastic bond model and reported adhesion measurements suggest that red-cell adhesion in Gaucher disease is not explained by total Lu/BCAM receptor abundance alone, and may depend more on receptor activation state.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that measured adhesion exceeds model predictions based on a 1.3-fold receptor increase; matching the reported adhesion requires more binding-competent receptors. Their sickle-cell analysis also models the reported hydroxyurea-associated change.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-and-assay study, not evidence of clinical outcomes or treatment benefit. The abstract gives no cohort size, and the inferred receptor-activation mechanism needs direct validation.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.75 entirely from three cross-lists. Broadest cross-listing among selected candidates; cross-listing indicates breadth, not readership. No independent HF/HN attention signal.

sections.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
sections.abstract: HERMES uses paired H&E and multiplex-immunofluorescence images with process-level supervision to generate auditable tumor-immune-microenvironment readouts.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across four colorectal-cancer field-level tasks, the authors report 84.5% average accuracy for HERMES (4B), versus 74.7% for the strongest of twelve compared models; they also report results on a CODEX cohort and head-and-neck cancer.
sections.unique_caveat: Model evaluation does not establish clinical validity or improved care. The abstract does not provide cohort sizes or prospective evaluation details.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.25 from one cross-list; recorded Semantic Scholar counts are 0 citations and 0 influential citations; no HF/HN attention signal. Selected for biomedical measurement relevance.

sections.title: One-Step Self-Assembling Lipopolymer Coatings Enable Direct Longitudinal Biosensing in Native Biological Matrices
sections.abstract: The authors describe a self-assembling antifouling coating for label-free digital biosensing in undiluted biological matrices, including time-resolved extracellular-vesicle measurements from lung-cancer cell models.
sections.claimed_contribution: Integrated optofluidic measurements reportedly quantify tetraspanin-positive extracellular-vesicle secretion from 2D and 3D lung-cancer cell models using 50 μL in 10 minutes without isolation or purification.
sections.unique_caveat: Demonstrations use cell models and assay matrices, not patient cohorts or clinical diagnostic endpoints; broader performance across biological samples remains to be established.
sections.ranking_evidence: Signal score 0.50 from two cross-lists; no HF/HN attention signal. Included for its direct biomolecular assay application.

sections.title: MambaSplit: Severity-Robust and Inference-Efficient Semantic Unmixing of Fluorescence Microscopy Image Data
sections.abstract: MambaSplit uses a state-space image encoder and convolutional decoder to separate overlapping fluorescence structures across varied mixing ratios.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across five datasets and nine mixing ratios, the authors report the best RI-PSNR in 11 of 15 dataset-severity combinations and 5.9× faster inference than their strongest baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are image-unmixing benchmark metrics, including computationally summed images; they do not establish improved biological interpretation or downstream experimental outcomes.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Atomistic protein modeling expands beyond single structures: BioEmu2 targets ensembles and time propagation, CORE assesses ensemble reliability, and CrypticFlow balances global accuracy with local geometry. Spatial and microscopy methods treat reconstruction as quantitative inference: GaLF-ST reconstructs spatial expression, MambaSplit separates overlapping signals, and HERMES supervises multimodal tissue readouts. Measurement methods seek dynamic readouts: the lipopolymer platform reports extracellular-vesicle sensing, while the Gaucher-disease paper links receptor state, adhesion modeling, and measurement. These are distinct computational and assay studies, not evidence of a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Compare BioEmu2's predicted slow kinetics with direct time-resolved biochemical or structural measurements. Test CORE and CrypticFlow prospectively on held-out targets with ligand-conditioned multi-state predictions and consistent geometry, accuracy, and uncertainty measures. Assess GaLF-ST, HERMES, MambaSplit, and the biosensor on external tissues, independently prepared microscopy mixtures, and blinded sample panels against orthogonal reference assays. Test the Gaucher-disease receptor-state hypothesis with direct measurements of phosphorylated or binding-competent Lu/BCAM and adhesion across a characterized donor cohort. These are research proposals, not clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This relevance-ranked snapshot has no independent-attention hits among the 16 papers. Computational protein modeling is the clearest shared thread, alongside spatial transcriptomics and measurement-focused biomedical methods; experimental and prospective validation remains the key evidence gap.
